summary: Charles Eliot (1862–1931) studied at Cheltenham College and Balliol College, Oxford (~1880–1885). Working in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he served at the Foreign Office (~1886–1904), University of Sheffield (~1905–1912), and University of Hong Kong (~1912–1918).
Charles Elliott (1776–1856) was an Indologist who worked for the East India Company (~1795–1827). He later served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1836–1856).

Charles Gabriel Seligman (1873–1940) studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School (~1892–1896). Working in history and archaeology, he held the chair of Ethnology at the University of London and the London School of Economics (1913–1934).

Charles Goodman works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard (completed by 2002) and served as an associate professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

Charles H. Long (1926–2020) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Dunbar Junior College and the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago (~1956–1974), UNC Chapel Hill (~1974–1987), Duke (~1980–1987), Syracuse (~1987–1991), and UC Santa Barbara (~1991–1996).

Charles Hallisey (b. 1953) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1981–1988). He held posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1988–1992), Harvard (1996–2001, 2007), and UW–Madison (2001, 2005).

Charles Henry Tawney (1837–1922) was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1856–1860). He held posts at Trinity College (1860), Presidency University (1866–1872, 1875–1892), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1880), and the India Office Library (1892/1893–1903).

Charles Li works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He held posts as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of British Columbia (attested 2020), at CNRS (attested 2023), and at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Charles Malamoud (b. 1929) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Lyon (~1965–1972) and as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1998).
Charles Oman (1860–1946) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at New College, Oxford (~1878–1882) and subsequently held an academic post at the University of Oxford from around 1883 to 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden (1864–1949) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Dulwich College (~1878–1883) and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1883–1887), later holding a post at SOAS University of London (~1917–1935).

Charles Philip Brown (1798–1884) studied at East India Company College and with traditional teachers. An Indologist and linguist, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and as Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1865–1879).

Charles Ramble (b. 1957) studied at Durham and Oxford under Michael Aris. Active in Tibetology and religious studies, he held posts at Tribhuvan University, Oxford (2000–2009), the University of Chicago (2008), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2009).

Charles Rieu (1820–1902) studied at Geneva and Bonn under Christian Lassen, Georg Freytag, and Johann Gildemeister. Working in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he served at the British Museum (from 1847) and Cambridge as Adams Professor of Arabic.

Charles Rockwell Lanman (1850–1941) studied at Yale, Berlin, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Whitney, Weber, and Roth. A linguist and Indologist, he taught at Johns Hopkins (~1876–1880) and served as a professor at Harvard University from 1880 to 1926.

Charles S. Prebish (b. 1944) studied at Case Western Reserve under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. A scholar of Buddhism and religion, he served on the faculty at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007) and later at Utah State University (~2007).

Charles Taliaferro (b. 1952) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, Harvard Divinity School, the University of Rhode Island, and Brown University, and served as a professor at St. Olaf College (~1985–2021).

Charles Taylor (b. 1931) studied at McGill University and Balliol College, Oxford. A philosopher, he held faculty posts at the Université de Montréal (~1961–1966), McGill University (~1961–1998 as Professor of Political Science), and Northwestern University (~2002–2012).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu (1933–1996) studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1960) and the University of Illinois System (~1964–1969). Specializing in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he held a post at Ohio University (~1968–1972).

Charles Wilkins (1749–1836) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kālinātha (~1778–1785). He founded The Asiatic Society in 1784, served in the East India Company, and was librarian at the India Office Library (~1801–1836).
